stated_evidence.permanent_checks_navigation: value (test): [`runLimitsContractTests`](../runner/Tests/PWRunnerCoreTests/LimitsContractTests.swift); value (test): [`compare`](../tests/suites/runner_abi_layout/limits.py); path (control): [`main`](../tests/suites/runner_c_worker_harness/harness.c); path (test): [`runOrderingTests`](../runner/Tests/PWRunnerCoreTests/OrderingTests.swift); boundary (control): [`main`](../tests/fixtures/worker_lifecycle/proceed_control.c); path (test): [`runWorkerClockTests`](../runner/Tests/PWRunnerCoreTests/WorkerClockTests.swift); path (test): [`proceed_without_host_release`](../tests/suites/runner_c_worker_harness/run.sh); boundary (test): [`terminal_erasure`](../tests/suites/runner_c_worker_harness/run.sh)
stated_evidence.behavioral_claim: wait_for_proceed decides expiry from a validated continuous sample before consulting release or cancellation. A pre-expiry sample can be followed by delayed scheduling and a late acknowledgement, and a release stored before expiry can be refused by an expired next sample; cancellation wins only when its load observes it. A sample below the origin or the last accepted sample fails closed without another clock, and a rejection during an earlier exec refuses later phases without another read. Each phase's measured wait is added to the exec plan once, in ticks, at acknowledgement. Refusal erases an accepted token buffer, publishes done and exits without a host exit request; cancellation erases and exits without adding done, acknowledgement or failure. This bounds the sampled refusal path, not native calls, descendant lifetime or total cleanup. Deterministic precedence, race-gate, sample and exclusion controls establish the order; native controls exercise the clock under deny-default profiles on the recorded machine; actual system sleep is untested. Production duration is value-checked.

entries.counting_rule: Continuous time from the worker origin before setup, shared by exec steps, including worker setup and intervening work but excluding each acknowledged release wait.
entries.scope: All exec steps sharing worker origin; actor-level ownership of pool not explicitly restated.
entries.boundary_consequence: Exhaustion refuses a later spawn with `exec_failed` and `ETIMEDOUT`, no `child_pid` and no sandbox attribution. An unusable sample refuses spawn with no errno, or after spawn records a local timing fault beside any native error; after a rejected sample, later spawns are refused. Blocking spawn and non-exec operations may outlast this allowance.
entries.enforcement_point: Worker checks before spawn and during timed observation; blocking spawn/non-exec work not preempted.

stated_evidence.behavioral_claim: pw_clock_start records the worker origin before setup; pw_timing_setup converts the allowance to a ceiling tick count before policy reading or application and refuses an invalid timebase or unrepresentable duration with exit 12. wait_for_proceed adds each phase's measured wait once with checked addition. Exec attempts receive an absolute cutoff independent of the host polling clock. A local timing fault after spawn triggers cleanup. Blocking spawn and non-exec operations are not preemptible here. The production default sits a nominal 5,000 ms below worker_sentinel_wait; test equipment may shorten it independently and the specimen worker_timeout_ms override does not move it. Compiled values agree with the host configuration. Deterministic native controls vary spawn latency, release exclusion, intervening work, exact exhaustion, every timing stage, arithmetic refusals and cleanup. Real short-budget plans preserve completed prefix and trailing file effects through host assembly and serialization.

entries.label: Exec child reap grace (`exec_reap_grace`)
entries.refusal_names: Not applicable: not a specimen admission row.
entries.counting_rule: Continuous-time allowance to confirm an exec child's exit after observation ends.
entries.scope: Each exec child's final exit-confirmation window; not whole cleanup.
entries.boundary_consequence: Expiry, an unusable sample or a wait error leaves reaping unconfirmed and supplies no invented exit status; an unusable clock still permits the immediate exit check. Failed group termination leaves only an immediate exit check. This is not a total cleanup runtime limit.
entries.enforcement_point: Worker nonblocking final reap checks; failed group kill leaves immediate check only.

stated_evidence.behavioral_claim: Final reaping uses nonblocking waitpid in a local continuous-time observation window. Failed group termination or unusable reap time permits only an immediate nonblocking reap, whose status is kept when it returns the child. The allowance does not bound native syscall duration or host descheduling. Controlled pending/EINTR waits exhaust the grace; kill, wait and local timing faults retain missing status. Every wait is required to be nonblocking.

entries.label: Runner removal teardown wait (`runner_remove_teardown_wait`)
entries.refusal_names: Not applicable: not a specimen admission row.
entries.counting_rule: Nominal wait for a removed BYOXPC service to disappear from launchd.
entries.scope: One BYOXPC removal that issued bootout; no wait if none issued.
entries.control: Fixed. No wait when the removal issued no bootout.
entries.boundary_consequence: A service still listed at expiry retains its cleanup record with a warning; a later `runner remove` or `runner reconcile` continues recovery.
entries.enforcement_point: Runner removal polls launchd service state, every 50 ms per coverage.

stated_evidence.behavioral_claim: After its own bootout, runner remove re-reads the service every 50 milliseconds until it is absent or the nominal allowance is spent. Controlled cleanup systems report the job present for two reads and then absent (completion after two waits), present for every read (retention after the whole allowance), and a skipped bootout (nothing awaited). The live removal cases observe real launchd teardown.

entries.label: External runner respawn throttle (`byoxpc_throttle_interval`)
entries.refusal_names: Not applicable: not a specimen admission row.
entries.counting_rule: Minimum launch spacing from previous launch, not previous exit.
entries.scope: Each generated external runner launchd job; interval measured from previous launch.
entries.control: Fixed in the generated plist. An installed plist can be edited by hand after `runner remove` and a fresh install; the registry's plist hash then differs and removal reports the ownership disagreement.
entries.boundary_consequence: Request arriving within interval waits remainder. Missing key means launchd ten-second default; occupied/retiring acquisition can retry without submission.
entries.enforcement_point: launchd job ThrottleInterval set by runner install.

stated_evidence.behavioral_claim: Measured on one owned installation (macOS 14.8, user scope) with the plist rewritten per candidate: with no key a run 0.4 s after the previous one took about 10.3 s and a run after the install's own verify about 9.2 s; with the interval at one second those took about 1.3 s and 0.3 s. The single-use live case reads the installed plist's value and waits it out plus a margin before requiring a fresh host.
